messages:
sam_sales: Hey team — AcmeHealth POC starts next week. They want LLM inference in their VPC. Question: should we push for PrivateLink or VPC peering for the POC? They care about client IP preservation for logging, minimal firewall changes, and want a rough pricing delta for our presales docs. POC target Mon. @ashley_netops @ben_secb @maria_engineer

ashley_netops: For a fast POC I usually recommend PrivateLink (interface endpoint) — avoids peering setup, no route table changes, and works across accounts. Pros: isolation, simple SG allowlist. Cons: endpoint hourly + data processing costs and slight ops to create endpoint service on our side.

ben_secb: Security notes: we need the customer's security questionnaire answers either way. PrivateLink reduces attack surface (no public IPs). We'll ask for: CIDR ranges for allowlist, intended subnet for endpoint, and whether they'll do TLS inspection. Also ask for SOC2 report and whether they require customer-managed KMS for logs.

maria_engineer: Technical detail on "client IP preservation": with PrivateLink traffic goes to the endpoint ENI in their VPC. On our side the connection appears from the endpoint network path — if you need original client IPs in app logs we can add X-Forwarded-For at the proxy/NLB layer. If they require TCP-level source-ip preservation for auth, peering is simpler (peer keeps source IPs).

ashley_netops: Quick checklist for each option:
- PrivateLink: customer creates Interface Endpoint -> you approve endpoint service (or we publish). Customer updates SG to allow outbound TCP/443 to endpoint. We provide NLB + SG details and service name. No route table changes.
- VPC Peering: create peering connection, update route tables, ensure no CIDR overlap, update security groups to allow peered CIDRs. No endpoint hourly fees but potentially more route/ops work.

ben_secb: Firewall snippet we usually share with customers (paste into their security doc):
```
# Customer SG (example)
Type: HTTPS  Protocol: TCP  Port: 443  Destination: <interface-endpoint-eni-subnet>  Description: Allow outbound to Redwood PrivateLink
# If using peering
Type: Custom TCP  Protocol: TCP  Port: 443  Destination: 10.64.0.0/16  Description: Allow outbound to Redwood peered VPC CIDR
```
We avoid publishing public IP blocks; we'll give the NLB ENI subnets during handoff.

sam_sales: Pricing ask from customer: high level numbers to justify decision for POC (we'll bill for hosting anyway). Any ballpark figures?

ashley_netops: Ballpark (very approximate):
- PrivateLink: endpoint interface ~$0.01/hr + data processing ~$0.01-0.02/GB (varies by region) on top of our per-token/throughput pricing.
- Peering: no endpoint hourly but normal VPC data transfer rates between AZs/accounts (~$0.01-0.02/GB).
For small POC traffic (GBs), cost delta is negligible — choose PrivateLink for speed.

maria_engineer: Test plan + curl example to validate once endpoint exists:
```
# from customer's bastion (example)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" https://api.redwood-internal.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# or use --resolve to point domain to endpoint ENI IP for TLS test
curl --resolve "api.redwood-internal.example:443:10.0.5.12" https://api.redwood-internal.example/
```
Include full request/response sample for our ops to verify.

sam_sales: Great. Action items: 1) Ashley to send PrivateLink service name + NLB SG template. 2) Ben to add security checklist items for questionnaire. 3) Maria to prepare quick smoke test script. I'll share with Acme.

deploy-bot: Notice: privatelink-service 'pl-svc-0a1b2c' created in account redwood-inference-prod, NLB targets pending verification.

ashley_netops: I'll DM the SG template and service name. Also ask Acme for the endpoint subnet(s) and whether they have TLS inspection; if they have inspection we may need to provide cert chain and consider mutual TLS.

ben_secb: Also, if they require egress logging to their SIEM, we'll provide connection logs + request IDs. Good to know now so we can include fields in our security questionnaire template.

sam_sales: Thanks all — I'll send a short handoff email to AcmeHealth with these notes and request the endpoint subnet + SOC2 copy. Will follow up with timeline. :thumbsup:
